svg.title: Lunar Love-number sensitivity by observable family
svg.desc: Which observable family is sensitive to the lunar Love numbers h2, k2 and l2, from a real run of engine v0.39.0 on scenarios/lunar-infrastructure-geodesy-sensitivity.toml. Each cell is the RMS partial derivative of a family's observations with respect to a parameter, in that family's own units (so cells are compared across a row, not down a column); a dash means the family has no sensitivity. laser ranging: h2 7.6, k2 none, l2 9.8. orbiter tracking: h2 none, k2 0.00086, l2 none. surface gravimeter: h2 2.9e+03, k2 4.3e+03, l2 none. surface clock: h2 2.8e-17, k2 2.8e-17, l2 none. With all four families, the Cramer-Rao sigma is 0.36 % of nominal h2, 0.52 % of k2 and 1.16 % of l2. Adding a family never lowered the smallest eigenvalue (28 of 28 additions), but the trace of the pseudo-inverse was no larger in only 16 of 28: that half of bar G3 is NOT MET. The orbiter family sees the line-of-sight integral of the k2 acceleration, an upper-end figure. MODELLED: a restricted three-body model with stated simplifications and illustrative inputs, not a measurement of any lunar quantity. Advisory: analysis output from a research and engineering tool, not type-approved navigation equipment and not a safety-of-life service.
